item.title: Florian Wirtz wants Germany to build off 5-0 win over the Netherlands
item.description: Photo by Getty Images | AFP via Getty Images Germany ended 2026 with a statement victory over the Netherlands in Berlin for the last group stage match in the UEFA Nations League. The result came just a few short days after Germany won 3-1 in Serbia and the Dutch handedly defeated Greece 7-0 in Amsterdam. The result is that Jürgen Klopp now has three wins under his belt as manager of the German national team and he was back to his unique blend of charisma, air-jumping, and fist-pumping as his side ran riot against the Dutch. What Mainz, Borussia Dortmund and Liverpool fans often saw on the touchlines was evident at the Olympiastadion, especially after Brajan Gruda scored Germany’s fifth and final goal of the match. Gruda’s strike came after Florian Wirtz’s brace and Nico Schlotterbeck’s goal that built on the 1-0 lead Germany brought into the halftime interval thanks to a lovely strike from Derry Scherhant. The result sees Germany finish top of Nations League Group B as they now await to see who they’ll face in the quarterfinals of the competition. But for the time being, Germany and Klopp have established a solid foundation to build from after two straight wins this international break. For Liverpool’s Wirtz, who was absolutely class in both the win over Serbia and the Netherlands, spoke post-match in Berlin about the importance of Die Mannschaft ’s momentum. “I would definitely say it’s a fitting end to the year, and we’re very happy with it. We want to build on this next year. We want to keep improving. I think we’ve definitely taken some good steps forward in our development as a team. I’m very proud and happy to be part of this team. It’s a real joy,” said Wirtz (via @iMiaSanMia ). Wirtz has four goals in Germany’s last five matches, though he only came on as a second half sub in the 1-0 loss at Greece back in September. For that occasion, he was only in the squad earlier than expected due to both Kai Havertz and Jamal Musiala suffering injuries in the 1-1 draw with the Netherlands. Liverpool fans will certainly be pleased with his form for Germany and hope that he can take it back to Merseyside as another testament to Klopp finding what makes a squad tick and capitalizing on their talents. As Wirtz alluded to after the full-time whistle, there’s a lot to build on for next year for Germany and every reason to believe Klopp can continue to nudge them in the right direction. item.title: UConn men’s basketball senior Solo Ball close to returning from wrist surgery
item.description: STORRS — UConn has reinforcements coming. Senior forward Solo Ball has been cleared to participate in full contact practice and is ramping up to make his return this season after having wrist surgery in the offseason, UConn announced on Monday. “Solo will use the next few weeks as a ramp-up period until he is fully ready to return to game action,” men's basketball coach Dan Hurley said in a statement. “We’re excited to bring him back into the fold this season. When the decision was initially made for Solo to take a medical redshirt this season, the 5-in-5 rules weren’t yet in place. After that significant development along with his tremendous progress in his rehab, we made the decision along with Solo and his family to bring him back this season.” Na'jai Hines breakout: UConn men's basketball's Na'jai Hines breaks out after Dan Hurley adjustment The Virginia native started 39 of 40 games last season, averaging 12.8 points and three rebounds per game. He tied for first in 3-point makes with 77. “I just think everyone’s just so happy for him because ... he needed to heal from what he went through,” Hurley said after Monday’s practice. “With a guy like Solo, you don't want the game to be taken away from him because he loves the game so much. He loves to compete so much. He loves his teammates so much, he loves UConn so much, and he just loves basketball so much. Not everyone's going to take missing that time as hard as a guy like Solo Ball can take.” Ball’s return to practice couldn’t have come at a better time for the Huskies. Starting forward Nik Khamenia injured his left foot in last week’s win over Wagner, sidelining him six to eight weeks. Talented freshmen Colben Landrew and Egor Amosov played well in place of Khamenia in Friday’s win over Ohio State, but adding a proven starter to an already loaded lineup will only help the Huskies going forward. There is not yet a timetable for which Ball will play his first game, and Hurley said he doesn’t want Khamenia’s injury to be a reason he rushes back to the court. “We want him to be feeling at his peak before he gets out there and feel pressured because of Nik’s situation because it really doesn’t address it,” Hurley said. Behind the scenes, Ball has been continuing to put in extra work to get back to the type of player he was last season. Ball’s shot count was shown on the screens of UConn’s practice facility, showing the senior shooting 957 shots within the last day. That was more than double of Amosov, who was second at 420. Yep, you read that right. item.title: "We had to adapt" – Klopp breaks down Germany's tactical approach to stun the Netherlands
item.description: "We had to adapt" – Klopp breaks down Germany's tactical approach to stun the Netherlands Putting the Netherlands to the sword 5-0 in Berlin this evening , Jürgen Klopp was bowled over by his team's ruthless performance which saw them top Nations League Group A2 “It was really extraordinary. The match was exceptionally difficult. Against a really good opponent, you have to find a way,” the DFB head coach said in an interview with ARD. "We had to adapt, had to change a few things — actually, some big things — and we made those changes, took a lot away from them and then scored some unbelievable goals. “It was madness. A great football match and a fantastic result. To be able to do that here in Berlin, in the last international match of the year, I wouldn't have dared to wish for that,” he said. Regarding the national team's tactical approach against the Netherlands this evening, the 59-year-old said his side had to tweak some tactics midway through the game. "In all the other matches, we were incredibly dominant. Today was intense in a completely different way. Both teams wanted to press high, and neither team did the other any favours. "Instead, they were playing the ball over each other's heads.We tried to keep things simple. Whenever we could play out quickly, that's what we wanted to do. "Otherwise, there was no point driving ourselves crazy. I thought we could leave the perfect build-up play against high pressing for another time. We'll do that when we have two weeks. "So we wanted to play towards Kai [Havertz] and compete for the second balls. When the ball was on the ground, they caused problems with Reijnders operating as a number ten. "Meanwhile, Malen occupied both centre-backs. They made us run. You have to be braver in those situations. You have to allow a defender to step out." “Either Jona [Tah] or Schlotterbeck had to step forward into midfield to defend. At that point, we started causing them problems,” Klopp explained with great detail. Two of Germany's least experienced attackers, Derry Scherhant and Brajan Gruda, were both singled out for praise by Klopp. He felt the duo put in a remarkable shift all night. "The work they put in, the work they had to do today, was brutal. That's what makes a team in the end, because other players can play football too. "But it's about what you put into it in terms of commitment and passion. That's what matters in the end. These lads are still surprising themselves." “Today we showed that we can also be devastating when attacking quickly. That's something we hadn't shown before,” Klopp concluded.

item.title: “I Had Surgery” – Frances Tiafoe’s Girlfriend Ayan Broomfield Reveals Health Struggles as She Travels to Support American at ATP Finals
item.description: Ayan Broomfield (left) and Frances Tiafoe (right), © Instagram/ayan.broomfield Frances Tiafoe’s girlfriend, Ayan Broomfield, has shared an update regarding an eye surgery she underwent recently. According to Broomfield, her recovery from the surgery is taking much longer than originally anticipated. However, she has decided at the last minute to join her American ATP star boyfriend in Turin, Italy, where he will be competing at the year-end ATP Finals. Broomfield, a former tennis player herself, took to her Instagram on Sunday, November 15, and wrote: “I had surgery 2 weeks ago on my eye and the recovery has been a lot tougher than expected but made the latest decision possible to fly out and see Foe so if you see my bloodshot eye… no you didn’t.” Frances Tiafoe’s girlfriend Ayan Broomfield’s Instagram Story (Source: Instagram/ayan.broomfield) Broomfield later confirmed she had reached Turin, where her boyfriend has been drawn in the Ivan Lendl Group alongside Carlos Alcaraz, Daniil Medvedev and Flavio Cobolli. It’s worth noting that Tiafoe is making his ATP Finals debut this year, and on paper, the American has a tough task on his hands in terms of progressing to the semifinals from the Round Robin phase. The World No. 8 has losing head-to-head records against Alcaraz and Medvedev, but he has so far dominated his rivalry with Cobolli . Frances Tiafoe arrived in Turin for the 2026 ATP Finals after losses in Shanghai, Vienna and Paris Tiafoe’s form has not been at its best coming into the 2026 ATP Finals. At this year’s last Major, the US Open, the American registered a semifinal finish and was widely expected to end the season on a high. However, since his run to the last four in New York in September, Tiafoe’s results have been underwhelming. In Tokyo, he ended ATP veteran Kei Nishikori’s career in the first round but then fell to a second-round loss to Arthur Fils of France, who is also in Turin for the ATP Finals. Next, at the Shanghai Masters, Tiafoe got past Yannick Hanfmann in the second round but lost a three-set thriller against eventual champion Alejandro Davidovich Fokina. Further losses awaited the American in Vienna and at the Paris Masters. In the Austrian capital, Lorenzo Musetti dashed his hopes of progress, while in Paris, home hope Quentin Halys downed him. It’s worth noting that Alcaraz, Tiafoe’s first opponent at the ATP Finals, won the Tokyo, Vienna and Paris titles, and is the favorite to win the year-end championships for the first time in his career this year. item.title: Eagles roster news: Giants poach practice squad player, plus more happenings
item.description: MINNEAPOLIS, MN - OCTOBER 19: Philadelphia Eagles wide receiver Xavier Gipson (87) warms up before the NFL game between the Minnesota Vikings and Philadelphia Eagles on October 19th, 2025, at U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis, MN. (Photo by Bailey Hillesheim/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles officially announced seven roster moves on Monday. In addition to these transactions, there were some more Eagles-related items listed on the NFL’s November 16 personnel notice. Here’s an overview: WR Hollywood Brown and OT Fred Johnson cleared waivers. WR Xavier Gipson was signed away from the Eagles’ practice squad to the New York Giants’ active roster. DT Leki Fotu had a tryout with the Eagles. WR Quentin Skinner had a free agent visit with the Eagles. Let’s sort through this news on a player-by-player basis. HOLLYWOOD BROWN and FRED JOHNSON These veterans are now free to sign with any team. The Eagles could add them back to their practice squad … but I’m guessing they’ll be looking for new NFL homes. Will be mildly interesting to see if they’re able to latch on anywhere. XAVIER GIPSON You may recall Gipson spent time as the Eagles’ punt returner in 2025 before a disastrous fumble in a loss to the Dallas Cowboys ultimately contributed to him getting cut. The Birds originally acquired him off waivers from the New York Giants. Then he returned to the Giants after being waived by Philly last year. Then he signed to the Eagles’ practice squad in September after New York cut him. Now the Giants are bringing him back to the Meadowlands. He must be well-versed with the New Jersey Turnpike by now. LEKI FOTU The 28-year-old Fotu is a 6’5”, 330 pound defensive tackle who’s made 26 starts in 66 career games played from 2020-2025. With the Eagles trading Jordan Davis to the Jacksonville Jaguars, the Birds have a need for more nose tackle depth. Fotu can help to fill that role, be it on the practice squad or the roster. QUENTIN SKINNER Skinner previously joined the Eagles’ practice squad on October 28 before getting cut on November 3. The Eagles could be interested in him providing some wide receiver depth.

item.title: Pro Padel debuts Nov. 18 at Dolby Live in Las Vegas
item.description: LAS VEGAS -- The Pro Padel League (PPL) makes its Las Vegas debut Wednesday, November 18 at Dolby Live at Park MGM, giving Las Vegas sports fans a first look at one of the world’s fastest-growing racket sports. Top pros from around the world will be on display for four days of competition culminating in the championship and third-place matches on Saturday. The women’s final will air live nationally on CNBC Saturday at 4 p.m. Pacific. All matches will stream on the league's YouTube channel . Las Vegas marks the last stop on the PPL’s four-event 2026 regular-season calendar. Founded in 2023, the PPL is North America’s professional padel league. It features 10 teams representing cities from the U.S., Canada and Mexico. Each team fields men’s and women’s doubles teams with results counting equally toward the team total. After the first three events, the DC Matrix lead the standings, followed by the Florida Goats and Mexico Waves. The Las Vegas Smash, winners of the inaugural PPL championship in 2023, sit in eighth place and need to have a big week to qualify for the league finals Dec. 3–6 in Miami. The Smash open the tournament Wednesday at 5 p.m. against the New York Atlantics before closing Thursday against San Diego. The Smash roster features two of the PPL's hottest players in Jimena Velasco and Águeda Pérez Ortiz. The two have produced 29 of the franchise’s 35 points and will need to produce if Vegas wants to advance. Velasco partnered with Raquel Eugenio Barrera to reach the women’s final at the league’s last stop in Playa del Carmen. “Las Vegas is one of the world’s premier sports and entertainment destinations, making it a natural fit for the Pro Padel League as we continue to grow the sport across North America,” said Mike Dorfman, CEO of the Pro Padel League. “With a global audience descending on the city for race week, we have a unique opportunity to introduce professional padel to new fans while connecting with international visitors who already know and love the sport. Between our partnership with MGM Resorts, bringing world-class competition to Dolby Live at Park MGM and showcasing padel along the iconic Bellagio Fountain Walk, we’re creating an experience that puts the sport front and center in one of the most exciting cities in the world.” Wait. item.title: Is that sarcasm? Jürgen Klopp says it was ‘incredibly difficult’ to humiliate the Netherlands
item.description: (Photo by Maja Hitij/Getty Images) | Getty Images Despite his country’s reputation, Germany coach Jürgen Klopp is known for a sense of humor. At both Borussia Dortmund and Liverpool FC, he would amuse fans and journalists with witty remarks and biting sarcasm. However, there are moments where Klopp seems like he is joking but is actually being serious. When he calls the 5-0 win over the Netherlands a difficult game, he means it. “What we’ve just witnessed was truly extraordinary,” the former LFC boss told reporters at full time (via @iMiaSanMia ).“ The game was extraordinary, and incredibly difficult.” “Against a really good opponent, you have to find a way to win,” he added. “We had to adapt and make a few adjustments, some fairly significant ones, but we made them. We took away a lot of their strengths. And then we scored some incredible goals. That was unbelievable.” “It was a fantastic football match and a wonderful experience. To be able to do this here in Berlin, in front of our home crowd, in the final international game of the year, is amazing.” This may be a trick he picked up from Pep Guardiola, back when the legendary pair were coaching against each other in the Premier League. Pep had a tendency to hype up his opponent to make a big win seem sweeter. Whether or not Klopp also did it with Liverpool, he’s probably sincere about his feelings regarding this game. This was the Netherlands worst defeat since 1959 (ironically, a 7-0 loss at the hands of the Germans) that capped off an otherwise disappointing year for Germany with a bit of a flourish. item.title: Grand Slam of Darts: Schedule, results & prize money
item.description: Luke Littler became world number one for the first time when he won the Grand Slam of Darts in 2025 [Press Association] The 2026 Grand Slam of Darts gets under way on Saturday, as another of the Professional Darts Corporation's (PDC) major titles is set to be won in Wolverhampton. This edition is bigger than ever, with 48 players taking part, and unlike most of darts' major tournaments, the players are split into groups in the initial phase, rather than a straight knockout format. Each player will face two opponents in their group, with only the group winner progressing into the last 16. The rest of the competition is a straight knockout format. Luke Littler is the defending champion following a 16-11 victory over Luke Humphries in the 2025 final to become world number one for the first time. Littler faces a tough start, with Beau Greaves his opponent on the opening evening, and Neils Zonneveld, who beat Littler in their only previous meeting, completing the group. When is the Grand Slam of Darts? The tournament lasts for nine days from Saturday, 14 November to Sunday, 22 November. Group stage (14-17 November) - 48 matches Second round (18-19 November) - eight matches Quarter-finals (20-21 November) Semi-finals (22 November) Final (22 November) What is the format? In the group stage, the format is best of nine legs, or first to five legs. In the initial phase, two points are awarded for a win, with the group winner progressing to the last 16. In case of players being level on points at the end of the group phase, the following tie-breakers apply: Total Leg Difference Total Legs Won Total Legs Won Against Throw Highest Total Tournament Average (to two decimal places) Highest Winning Match Average (to two decimal places) A play-off - nine-dart leg Second-round matches are a best-of-19 format, or first to 10 legs. The quarter-finals, semi-finals and final are best of 31 legs, or first to 16 legs. Who is playing and how did they qualify? With the tournament expanded, a new set of qualification rules have been put in place. Up to 24 players could qualify from reaching a major PDC televised final in the past 12 months, but only nine ended up qualifying via that route, partly because of the dominance Littler has shown. Ten players reached Wolverhampton from the PDC youth, development and challenge tours, the Women's Matchplay and Women's Series and championships from across the globe. Six more secured places through the European Tour, while 13 qualified with a Players Championship win. The final 10 spots, which include ninth seed Stephen Bunting, were claimed in a PDC tour card holder qualifying event. From there, the top-16 ranked players in the PDC's order of merit were seeded and filled pot one. The next 16 went into pot two and the final 16 made up pot three. One player from each pot was then allocated to a group. Grand Slam of Darts groups, order of play & results Afternoon sessions start at 13:00 GMT, with evening sessions at 19:00 (19:30 on 15).

item.title: Germany vs Netherlands: The tactics board - Jurgen Klopp’s verticality shreds the Oranje in Berlin demolition
item.description: Germany v Netherlands - UEFA Nations League 2026/27 Group A2 MD6 - Getty Images Sport Germany secured a dominant 5-0 victory over the Netherlands in the UEFA Nations League, powered by a tactical masterclass in vertical transitions and high-pressing. Jurgen Klopp's side exploited defensive gaps to dismantle Xavi Hernandez's structure in a second-half rout. Jurgen Klopp’s Germany delivered a definitive tactical statement at the Olympiastadion, overwhelming the Netherlands with a 5-0 victory that married structural discipline with explosive transitional play. The objective for Klopp was clear: implement a high-intensity counter-press to disrupt the Netherlands' technical build-up and utilise the half-spaces to isolate the Dutch full-backs. By maintaining a compact 4-2-3-1, Germany looked to force turnovers in the middle third and immediately flood the box with runners. Xavi Hernandez, seeking to secure top spot in the group, set his side up to control the tempo through possession. Missing key figures like Frenkie de Jong, the Oranje aimed to use their double pivot to bait the German press before finding Cody Gakpo and Donyell Malen in wide areas. However, the Dutch tactical plan lacked the necessary defensive coverage to handle Germany’s speed of transition, ultimately leading to a catastrophic collapse in the second half as their structural integrity evaporated under sustained pressure. Germany's tactical setup Germany deployed a fluid 4-2-3-1 formation that prioritised verticality and central overload. Aleksandar Pavlovic acted as the primary metronome in the pivot, allowing Joshua Kimmich to vacate his nominal right-sided role to create numerical superiorities in the final third. This was evident for the opening goal in the 41st minute, where Kimmich’s positioning helped facilitate Denis Scherhant’s breakthrough. The pressing triggers were meticulously coached; Germany allowed the Dutch centre-backs, Jan Paul van Hecke and Micky van de Ven, time on the ball but aggressively swarmed as soon as a pass was directed toward the Oranje wingers or the retreating Tijjani Reijnders. In possession, Germany’s shape often resembled a 3-2-5, with one full-back tucking in to form a back three, providing security against the Dutch counter-attack. item.title: Klopp hails Germany squad after dominant Netherlands win: "This is a very special group"
item.description: Klopp hails Germany squad after dominant Netherlands win: "This is a very special group" Germany rounded off 2026 in stunning fashion in Berlin, as they dismantled the Netherlands 5-0 to seal top spot in their Nations League group. Derry Scherhant opened the scoring shortly before half-time, before a Florian Wirtz brace and goals from Nico Schlotterbeck and Brajan Gruda rounded off a memorable evening. Following the final whistle, boss Jürgen Klopp reflected on his first six matches in charge, offering an assessment of the expectations that came alongside his summer arrival. “I had a bit of a feeling in the summer that people thought the new coach, which was me, would have to drink himself into believing the German national team was good,” he said in his post-match interview with ARD. But he was keen to emphasise just how impressed he has been by the players involved, suggesting that the public perception does not reflect the quality within the German ranks. "They are wonderful footballers, wonderful, fantastic characters. But the perception from outside isn't like that, because apparently we're constantly chasing something. "I'm not chasing anything. I'm at the beginning. I don't feel as though I've already been through three tournaments. I simply feel that this is a great team. “We have pretty good quality, and if we get these highly talented players going, then it won't be much fun playing against us.” That was most certainly the case for the Netherlands, who saw the game continue to drift out of their sight as Germany romped home in the second half. “This is a very special group at the moment,” added Klopp. "I know people have heard that a few times before, and our responsibility is to make that visible and keep it visible. “We can't change the world, but we can show a positive face, and that's what we did today. I think everyone who was here today will go home with a smile on their face and won't question the German national team for at least three or four months.” The new boss also spoke on the privilege of representing his country after his remarkable club career. "I've had the great fortune of coaching three big clubs, and I could always identify with those clubs very easily. During my time at each club, there was no other club for me. I loved working there. “And now I have the great fortune of working for my home country. There's nothing greater, and that's exactly how it felt.” He was though, adament that Germany cannot get carried away after the result, acknowledging that further improvement will be needed when his side return to action in March. "Now we have the opportunity to play in the quarter-finals. I've had a look, and there are only really tough opponents in there. I'm already looking forward to it. “But to say we've suddenly solved all our problems would obviously be nonsense. We've shown something, though, and that was important.”

item.title: Wirtz feels the fun as Germany run riot over Netherlands
item.description: Germany's Florian Wirtz celebrates his side's big win over the Netherlands in Berlin. (Odd ANDERSEN) Florian Wirtz scored twice and Brajan Gruda contributed a goal and two assists as Germany cruised to a 5-0 win over the Netherlands in Berlin to reach the Nations League quarter-finals on Monday. Derry Scherhant and Nico Schlotterbeck also got on the scoresheet as the Germans cut the visitors to shreds in the most impressive match of Jurgen Klopp's six-game stint as coach. It was Germany's biggest win over their neighbours since a 7-0 victory in 1959. "The game was outstanding," Klopp told German broadcaster ARD. "We scored unbelievable goals. It was just insane. A fantastic football match and a magnificent experience. I wouldn't have even dared to wish for all of this." Klopp singled out Gruda and Scherhant, two players he has given their debuts, for special praise. "Boy can those two play. But the amount of work they put in, it's immense. That's what defines a team -- and plenty of others can play football too." So often criticised for a lack of end product since his big-money move to Liverpool in 2025, Wirtz has scored in four in his past four games for Germany. "We hope that we can make it fun for the fans. It was definitely fun for us, especially in the second-half," Wirtz told ARD. The Dutch defeat was the first since their coach Xavi Hernandez took charge but, despite Greece's 1-0 win over Serbia on Monday, they also qualified for the final eight, although the last German goal dropped them to second in the group. The Netherlands offered little in attack after Germany's second and missed injured captain Virgil van Dijk at the back, with the hosts cutting through a flimsy defence at will. "I'm really sad, because before the game I was really proud," Xavi told reporters. "Today it was not about the football, but about speed and about (our) values." "I want to say sorry to our supporters, because today we showed our worst face. It's part of the process... We need to keep going and work on our values." - A 'final': Klopp - Germany knew only a victory would give them a realistic chance of reaching the quarters, with coach Klopp describing the match as a "final." In a corresponding move, the Lions released cornerback Nick Whiteside from the 53-man roster. At cutdowns in 2025, the Lions claimed Wheat off waivers and placed him on their active roster. Wheat was active for 15 games, though he was mainly a special teamer, playing 215 snaps in the third phase of the game and only 66 on defense. While his opportunities were minimal, he made the most of them, registering career highs in tackles (15), sacks (1.5), QB Hits (2), and PFF grade (82.3). Wheat left the Lions in free agency to re-join the Cowboys —the team that drafted him—but has been limited to just five games played with minimal production (three tackles). The Cowboys released him on November 14th to make room for defensive lineman Jonathan Bullard, and the Lions—having just lost Aidan Hutchinson to injury—were quick to claim him. With Wheat’s experience as a rush end in the Lions scheme, expectations are that he’ll get up to speed with the playbook quickly and could be incorporated into game action as soon as this weekend. While well-versed in the Lions system, expectations should reflect his involvement from last season: a core special teamer who can, on average, give the Lions 4-5 snaps a game on defense. item.title: PGA Tour outlines pathway details for developmental system
item.description: In June, PGA Tour CEO Brian Rolapp unveiled the circuit’s new competitive model with two series and a focus on promotion and relegation. On Monday, the Tour’s policy boards approved the fine print of that promotion and relegation system. At the year’s final meeting, the policy boards approved: Key elements of the circuit’s developmental programs; A new, performance-based priority ranking that puts every player in the developmental system on a single points list; Transition-year eligibility for the circuit’s Challenger Series and Korn Ferry Tour in 2027 before the circuit moves to the two-tier model in ’28. “For the last 18 months, the Future Competition Committee has worked to design the best version of the PGA Tour,” Rolapp said in a statement. “By creating a more connected, merit-based developmental system, there is a clear and open path for emerging talent to pursue their dreams.” Along with the new, unified priority ranking that combines all players in the Tour’s development system, the program also dramatically expands opportunities for college players via the PGA Tour University system. Nos. 6 through 25 on the final PGA Tour U points list at the end of the college season will earn status on the Korn Ferry Tour for the remainder of the current season and the following year. The revised system also provides access for college underclassmen via the PGA Tour U Accelerated program directly to the Challenger Series. The Korn Ferry Tour, which will be the primary pathway to the PGA Tour, will feature a 20-event schedule (down from 24 events this year), with 144-man fields and $1 million purses, which is the same as the current threshold. The schedule will be designed for a balance of events to be held before and after the NCAA Men’s Championship to provide PGA Tour U players opportunities to finish the season. Status on the Korn Ferry Tour will be primarily through a “unified priority ranking,” with the top 75 players at the end of the season, not otherwise exempt on the PGA Tour Championship Series or PGA Tour Challenger Series, exempt onto the secondary circuit. The new promotion program will also include Q-School, with the top 5 players earning status into PGA Tour Challenger Series events and the next 25 players and ties exempt onto the Korn Ferry Tour. Additionally, the board approved transition-year eligibility in 2027 for both the Challenger Series and Korn Ferry Tour, with various adjustments added to fill fields in 2028 for players who finish outside the top 175 on next year’s FedExCup Fall list. In relation to the post-playoff season, a “last chance” series, which will replace the FedExCup Fall, will include at least four events and will be played after the Tour Championship, with the top three finishers at the end of the series earning status into the next season’s Championship Series.
